reference.title: Push-Up Plus
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be read at authoring time, so the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Breathe in on the way down, breathe out as you press up and push into the plus.
breathing.cadence: About 1.6 s down, 1 s up, 0.6 s plus

prescription.tempo: 1.6 s down, 1 s up, 0.6 s plus, 0.4 s hold
prescription.progression: Slower plus with a longer hold, then feet elevated

cues.text: High plank: hands a little wider than the shoulders, body in one straight line, on the balls of the feet.
Lower as one piece, elbows about 30-45 degrees from the body, chest to a few cm above the floor.
Brief pause just above the floor, body straight.
Press back up to straight arms.
Keep the arms straight and push the floor away: the shoulder blades spread apart and the upper back rounds slightly up.
Hold the plus for a moment.
Let the shoulder blades settle back to the plank position, then the next rep.

mistakes.fix: Finish every rep by pushing the shoulder blades apart with straight arms.

mistakes.mistake: Bending the elbows in the plus
mistakes.fix: The plus comes from the shoulder blades, not the arms.
Squeeze the glutes and brace: the body stays in one line.
Push the floor away and down, not up toward the ears.
Pause in the plus before you lower.

kinematics.peak: ≈130° at the bottom (chest 11 cm above the floor); ≈13° in the plus
kinematics.norm: Straight at the top to about 90 degrees or more at the bottom (common coaching standard)

kinematics.peak: Plus: protraction 26°, upper back 4.8 cm higher with straight arms
kinematics.norm: Neutral in the plank; spread apart (protracted) in the plus; the push-up plus gives high serratus anterior activity relative to the upper trapezius (Ludewig 2004)
One straight line from head to heels (common coaching standard)
A little wider than the shoulders (Kim 2016 compared palm widths)

kinematics.peak: 1.6 s down, 0.3 s pause, 1.0 s up, 0.6 s into the plus, 0.4 s hold, 0.5 s settle
kinematics.norm: Controlled, with a short hold in the plus (clinical opinion)

sources.title: Ludewig, Hoff, Osowski, Meschke and Rundquist 2004, relative balance of serratus anterior and upper trapezius muscle activity during push-up exercises (Am J Sports Med 32(2):484-493)
Ekstrom, Donatelli & Soderberg 2003, surface electromyographic analysis of exercises for the trapezius and serratus anterior muscles (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 33(5):247-258)
Kim, Kim and Ha 2016, effect of the push-up exercise at different palmar width on muscle activities (J Phys Ther Sci 28(2):446-449; PMC4792988)

Wurm, VanderZanden, Spadavecchia, Durocher, Bickham, Petushek and Ebben, kinetic analysis of several variations of push-ups (ISBS 2010 conference proceedings; peak hand force 64% of body mass for a regular push-up, 70% and 74% with the feet on 30.5 cm and 61 cm boxes)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Wrist discomfort: use push-up handles or fists, or do the move on the knees.
modify: Knees on the floor (knee push-up plus).
Hands on a bench (incline push-up plus).
regressions: Plank scapular push-up (the plus without the push-up).

muscleNotes.pec_r: Main mover: lower and press the body.
muscleNotes.pec_l: Main mover: lower and press the body.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Main mover of the plus: pull the shoulder blades forward around the ribs (protraction); high activity with a low upper trapezius ratio in the push-up plus (Ludewig 2004).
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Main mover of the plus: pull the shoulder blades forward around the ribs (protraction); high activity with a low upper trapezius ratio in the push-up plus (Ludewig 2004).
muscleNotes.core: Holds the body in one straight line.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Stop the hips sagging or twisting.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Stop the hips sagging or twisting.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Control the shoulder blades as they move back and forth.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Control the shoulder blades as they move back and forth.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Squeeze to keep the hips in line.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Squeeze to keep the hips in line.
